deep.reconstruction:
Context. This folio is a working draft of the closing section of Riemann's 1859 Monatsbericht paper 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse'. That section derives the explicit formula for f(x). In modern terms f(x) = J(x) = sum over prime powers p^n <= x of 1/n. The previous folio contains a 'Nachtrag' and a cover letter in which Riemann asks to replace the last part of the paper with a rewritten version. This page is very likely that rewritten ending, or its draft. The top third is scratch work. The rest is a fair text that is nearly word-for-word the published ending.

A. Scratch (top of page).
(1) Starting point: f(y) = (1/2πi) ∫_{a-i∞}^{a+i∞} (log ζ(s)/s) y^s ds, with a > 1. This is the Mellin/Perron inversion of log ζ(s)/s = ∫_1^∞ f(x) x^{-s-1} dx.
(2) Gauss product for Π(s) = Γ(s+1):
  log Π(s) = lim_{m→∞} [ -Σ_{n=1}^m log(1+s/n) + s log m ].
  Hence -log Π(s/2) = lim [ Σ_{n=1}^m log(1+s/(2n)) - (s/2) log m ].
  Dividing by s and differentiating in s kills the term linear in s, so the derivative is a convergent series: d/ds[(1/s) log Π(s/2)] = -Σ_{n≥1} d/ds[(1/s) log(1+s/(2n))].
(3) The model term ∫ d/ds[(1/s) log(1-s/β)] x^s ds. Key identity:
  ∂/∂β [(1/s) log(1-s/β)] = 1/((β-s)β).
  For Re s > Re β the contour integral of x^s/((β-s)β), up to sign, equals x^β/β.
  x^β/β = ∫_0^x t^{β-1} dt if Re β > 0, or ∫_∞^x t^{β-1} dt if Re β < 0.
  Integrating in β gives Li(x^β) = ∫_0^x t^{β-1}/log t dt in one case and ∫_∞^x t^{β-1}/log t dt in the other.
(4) A side note e^{s log y} = 1 + s log y + ..., presumably about the behaviour of y^s near s = 0.

B. Fair text.
(i) Why integrate by parts first. Riemann proposes to substitute the Hadamard-type factorisation
  log ζ(s) = (s/2) log π - log(s-1) - log Π(s/2) + Σ_α log(1 + (s-1/2)²/α²) + log ξ(0).
  Here ξ(t) is his entire function with s = 1/2 + it. Term by term, the resulting integrals would not converge at ±i∞. So he first integrates by parts:
  f(x) = -(1/2πi)(1/log x) ∫_{a-i∞}^{a+i∞} d/ds[log ζ(s)/s] x^s ds.
  The transcription writes ξ here; read ζ.
(ii) Every term becomes ±(1/2πi)(1/log x) ∫ d/ds[(1/s) log(1-s/β)] x^s ds. This uses the Gauss product to write -d/ds[(1/s) log Π(s/2)] = Σ_n d/ds[(1/s) log(1+s/(2n))].
  - Terms linear in s, namely (s/2) log π and -(s/2) log m, give constants after division by s. They vanish on differentiation.
  - The constant term gives (1/2πi)(1/log x) ∫ (log ξ(0)/s²) x^s ds = log ξ(0), since the residue of x^s/s² at 0 is log x.
(iii) The model integral. Use ∂_β[(1/s) log(1-s/β)] = 1/((β-s)β). For a > Re β, close the contour to the left (x > 1); the only pole is s = β:
  -(1/2πi) ∫ x^s ds/((β-s)β) = x^β/β.
  This equals ∫_∞^x t^{β-1} dt if Re β < 0, and ∫_0^x t^{β-1} dt if Re β > 0.
(iv) Undo the integration by parts and integrate in β:
  +(1/2πi)(1/log x) ∫ d/ds[(1/s) log(1-s/β)] x^s ds = -(1/2πi) ∫ (1/s) log(1-s/β) x^s ds.
  This equals ∫_∞^x t^{β-1}/log t dt (+const) when Re β < 0, and ∫_0^x t^{β-1}/log t dt (+const) when Re β > 0.
(v) Fixing the constants.
  - In the first case, let Re β → -∞: both sides tend to 0, so the constant is 0.
  - In the second case, the integral ∫_0^x along complex paths with positive or negative argument differs by 2πi. On the respective path it tends to 0 as Im β → +∞ (respectively -∞). This fixes the branch of log(1-s/β) on the left so that the constant vanishes.
(vi) Assembly.
  - The β = 1 term from -log(s-1) gives +Li(x).
  - Each zero pair β = 1/2 ± iα gives -[Li(x^{1/2+αi}) + Li(x^{1/2-αi})].
  - The β = -2n terms give Σ_n ∫_x^∞ t^{-2n-1}/log t dt = ∫_x^∞ dt/((t²-1) t log t).
  - The constant term gives log ξ(0).
  Result: f(x) = Li(x) - Σ_α [Li(x^{1/2+αi}) + Li(x^{1/2-αi})] + ∫_x^∞ dt/((t²-1) t log t) + log ξ(0).
  Here α runs over the roots of ξ(t) = 0 with positive real part, ordered by size. The final remark stops after '...leicht zeigen, dass bei'. In print this becomes the statement that, with this ordering, the conditionally convergent series has a definite limit, while a different ordering could give any real value. The draft's last line, '; durch veränderte Anordnung aber würde sie jeden beliebigen reellen Werth erhalten können', is that ending.
errors: Scratch version (top of page): '1/(2πi)∫ x^s ds/((β-s)β) = x^β/β' lacks the minus sign. Riemann corrects it in the fair text ('-1/(2πi)∫ ...').

Scratch: the labels 'im ersten / im zweiten Falle' (Li(x^β) first, ∫_∞^x second) are attached before the cases are defined. They are the reverse of the order used in the fair text (first case Re β < 0 → ∫_∞^x; second case Re β > 0 → ∫_0^x). This is harmless bookkeeping.

Constant term (known issue, inherited by the published paper). Riemann replaces log(1+(s-1/2)²/α²) by log[(1-s/β)(1-s/β̄)]. These differ by the nonzero constant log(1+1/(4α²)). Likewise -log(s-1) differs from -log(1-s) by a constant (a choice of log(-1)). Constant/s terms do not vanish after the d/ds step; they contribute constants to f(x). So 'log ξ(0)' in Riemann's notation (ξ at t=0, i.e. s=1/2: ξ ≈ 0.4971, log ≈ -0.6990) is not literally the correct constant, which is -log 2 ≈ -0.6931. This discrepancy is discussed in the literature (e.g. Edwards, Riemann's Zeta Function). The branch discussion in (v) only partly addresses the issue.

Unjustified steps (standard for Riemann): termwise integration of the conditionally convergent sum over zeros, and convergence of Σ_α Li(x^ρ) in the stated ordering. Riemann only asserts these ('lässt sich ... leicht zeigen'). Rigorous proof came with von Mangoldt (1895).
The sentence beginning 'Es lässt sich ... dass bei' is left unfinished on this sheet.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the draft or revised ending of the published 1859 paper; the formulas and wording match the printed text almost verbatim. The only historically interesting points are documentary. It shows Riemann rewrote the last section (per the 'Nachtrag' letter on the previous folio). The scratch work shows his differentiate-in-β trick in rough form. No new mathematics beyond the published paper.
